segments.line: And at first, it's amazing.
On Tuesday, there's a maths test.
You don't know question four.
But Priya, two desks away, does.
'Twelve point five. Easy. '
You write down twelve point five.
You feel a bit bad.
You get an A.
After school, you want a second- hand game. The man in the shop says, 'Forty. Final price.
' And in his head: 'I'd take twenty. I just want it gone. '
You say twenty. He sighs. 'Fine. ' Then he thinks, 'Clever kid. '
Mo works it out by Wednesday. 'How did you know I was going to say that? '
So you tell him. He doesn't believe you, so you tell him exactly what he's thinking, right now. He goes very quiet.
'Okay. Never do that again. Also... do Priya. ' So you do.
At lunch, Priya looks over at Mo and thinks, 'Why is he always staring at me? ' Then: 'He's kind of funny, though. '
You tell Mo. Mo walks over and says hi.
Mo's face goes the colour of a tomato.
For the first time in two years, she says hi back.
On Thursday night, the family plays cards. Mum is thinking, 'Two kings. Don't smile.
' Ellie is thinking, 'I have no idea what game this is. '
You win four rounds in a row. Mum narrows her eyes. 'Are you cheating?
' 'No, ' you say. And technically, you're not.
Your mum's birthday is easy. She has been thinking about the same pair of blue boots for a week.
When she opens the box, she cries. 'How did you know? ' You just shrug.
By Friday, Mo has a plan. 'We could be detectives. Lost dogs. Lying boyfriends. Who stole the teacher's mug. '
He writes a price list on the back of his hand. Five dollars a question. Ten for the truth.
You laugh.
And then, on Saturday, your mum takes you and Ellie to the shopping centre.
And you stop laughing.
